Section 01 — Overview

Homepage & Introduction

📡

About the Tour

The ELEC014.23 Educational & Industry Tour brought CCS students to the Mindanao Media Hub — one of Mindanao's premier media and broadcasting facilities. The visit offered students a firsthand look at how media technology, digital production, and broadcasting systems operate in a professional environment.

📍

Tour Overview

The program was a single-day activity combining an industry tour of the Mindanao Media Hub in the morning and an afternoon seminar held at the ITRC (2nd Floor) of UIC. It was designed to bridge academic knowledge with real-world media and technology industry practices.

🎯

Course Objectives

ELEC014.23 aims to equip students with a realistic understanding of the IT and computing industry. Through direct industry exposure, students are expected to align their academic skills with market needs and professional expectations.

💡

Relevance to the Course

Seminars and workshops supplement classroom discussions on software engineering, networking, AI, and data systems — grounding theoretical concepts in observable, current industry practice.

🌐

Purpose of the Program

To foster professional readiness among CCS students by immersing them in authentic workplace settings, exposing them to contemporary technologies, and establishing meaningful connections with industry professionals.

📋

Program Outcomes

Students are expected to document insights, reflect on learnings, and produce this e-journal as a final examination output — demonstrating both technical understanding and reflective thinking on industry exposure.

Section 04 — Industry

Company & Industry Profile

Mindanao Media Hub

The Mindanao Media Hub is a leading media and broadcasting organization based in Davao City, serving as a central hub for news production, digital content creation, and media distribution across Mindanao and beyond.

The facility operates a full-scale broadcasting infrastructure, housing television and radio production studios, digital newsrooms, editing suites, and transmission systems — all managed by a team of media professionals, engineers, and content creators.

The Hub plays a vital role in the local media landscape by producing news, public affairs programming, and digital content that inform and engage communities throughout the Mindanao region.

Key Technologies & Innovations Observed:

  • Broadcast Engineering
  • Digital Newsroom
  • Video Production
  • Live Streaming
  • Media Encoding
  • Radio Broadcasting
  • Content Management
  • Digital Editing
  • Transmission Systems
  • Social Media Integration
📖
Section 05 — Learnings

Student Reflections & Learnings

The visit to the Mindanao Media Hub was an experience that genuinely shifted my perspective on what technology looks like outside the classroom. Seeing the actual infrastructure behind broadcasting — the cameras, transmission equipment, editing suites, and the way everything is coordinated in real time — made me realize how much engineering and systems thinking goes into something as seemingly simple as a news broadcast.

The afternoon seminar was equally eye-opening, especially the talk on blockchain. I had encountered the concept in our coursework, but hearing it explained through analogies and real-world relevance made the ideas click in a different way. Understanding blockchain not just as a technology but as a system of trust and accountability gave me a new lens for looking at how digital information can be secured and verified.

Overall, this tour and seminar reminded me that the skills we are building in CCS are not abstract — they are directly connected to industries, systems, and communities that people depend on every day. That realization is motivating in a way that no lecture alone could replicate.

VL
Vinze Jerhald J. Lulab
BSIT-2A — ELEC014.23

Section 08 — Closing

Conclusion & Acknowledgments

The ELEC014.23 Educational & Industry Tour proved to be a significant milestone for students of the College of Computer Studies. The combined experience of attending expert seminars, engaging in interactive workshops, and observing real-world technology operations provided a depth of learning that extends far beyond the classroom.

Students returned with sharpened perspectives on software development, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and cloud computing — and more importantly, with a clearer sense of purpose and direction in their academic and professional journeys.

The program's success is owed to the collective effort of the faculty, coordinators, student committees, and the generous support of our industry partners who opened their doors and shared their expertise without reservation.
